results: You inherited a single Gem (500gp), cold and brittle, from a long-dead relative. It arrived with a warning: squander your newfound riches, and a debt long thought forgotten would be called in.
A distant cousin left you a small inheritance. Take 20gp and a Strange Compass (pretty) that always points towards something deep in the Wood.
You carry a hand-drawn Portrait (pretty) of a past love who disappeared into the Wood long ago. Somehow you know that they are still alive.
You found a Tiny Crystal Prism (pretty) buried in the dirt. When held up to the light, it shows visions of an unknown location deep within the Wood. Sometimes you feel a presence looking back at you.
You once freed a Nixie from a choked stream. In return, it gave you some Silver Moss (pretty). Swallow it near water, and the creature will come, once, to repay its debt.
You inherited an old Journal, bound in bark. Each evening, its pages are filled with the events of the day, crassly written from the journal's perspective. The writing is crude but accurate.
You protect a long-dormant family secret. Take a Locket (pretty) and an Ancient Key (pretty). They say that if joined with its twin, it opens a Gate through the Wood.

You received a Letter (pretty) detailing incontrovertible proof that your true parentage is that of the nobility. The note also indicates a date and location where you are to meet the letter's author, deep in the Wood.
You owe a great debt to a member of the nobility and carry their Signet (pretty), which serves as proof of their protection as well as your obligation.

You consumed a Mischievous Spirit that wreaths havoc on your insides, demanding to be taken home, deep in the Wood. It occupies one slot but absorbs one fatigue each day. It wants you alive (for now).
A roaming storyteller once spun you tales of great treasure hidden deep in the Wood. You thought it naught but fancy, till they gave you a Rolled-up Map (pretty) marked with an X.
During your travels, you met a dying hunter who asked you to deliver a message to their loved ones. Take a Letter (pretty), sealed with tree sap. It is addressed only to the Lord of Winter.
You found a wounded beast in the forest but chose to ignore it. You see it everywhere now, but only when you're alone. It looks sad but not angry. You cannot become panicked when alone.
You promised a childhood friend that you'd bring them back a rare gift, something unique in all of the world. Take a Bracelet (pretty) woven from twine and wildflowers.
You crossed a creature of the Wood, and it cursed you with a Stone Heart. With each passing month, the stone grows heavier by one slot. Until your debt is lifted, you cannot truly die.
You carved a Whistle (pretty) from an Oak Lord's branch. Your act did not go unnoticed. You cannot seem to rid yourself of the whistle either.
The Dawn Brigade did your family a service, giving you a dried Blood-Red Flower (pretty) as proof. When the flower turns white, it means the favor is owed.
An entertainer once visited your home, filling it with story and song. He left the next morning with the Twig (pretty) in your hand. You believe it brings you luck. It smells faintly of sulfur.
One of your ancestors wronged a Moss Witch, who cursed their bloodline. Your visage causes mirrors to shatter. You've noticed that the shards can sometimes reveal illusions.

The once rich waters of a life-giving river have turned black and putrid, rotting the land and sickening those who drink from it. A village elder points to some recent desecration as the cause, but most do not heed their words.

It feels like winter has arrived too quickly this year. Frost and snows paint their appearance much earlier than expected. There is a smell of iron to the frost found in windows, ponds, and cracks in the ground. It almost looks like a map.
A thick, unnatural fog has begun encroaching upon an ancient and holy tree. It is said to be the work of a great forest spirit, angered by nearby deforestation.

The night sky glows dimmer each evening, as if stars are disappearing one by one. Rumors of hellish creatures capturing farmers and pulling them into the Roots are spreading like wildfire. Village elders believe the two are connected.
The songbirds of the Wood have fallen eerily silent as of late. Hunters claim that a spectral figure has been spotted wandering the forest, igniting only an avenging encounter.

Strange, tear-shaped stones have been found throughout the region, sparking a 'gold rush' of sorts for jewelers and thieves alike. The locals believe they are the tears of the earth itself, weeping for a great tragedy yet to come.
Swarming pests gnaw away at the edges of doors, and farmers speak of a loud buzzing sound emanating from deep within the Wood. They say that the sound is getting closer.
The moon turns a deep crimson, bathing the night in an eerie, blood-red glow. Stray whispers of a divide between realms as at its weakest in centuries and fear what may emerge from the other side.
A right-blooming flower once thought extinct is sprouting up throughout the Wood. Its scent is intoxicating but also causes vivid nightmares.
Local livestock have grown increasingly agitated and unmanageable as of late. An old shepherd says it is due to an unsettling howl that emanates from the Wood each full moon.

Swarm of insects are fleeing from the Wood in droves, destroying any flowers and structures they come across. The sound of their wings has a familiar tune as they pass overhead, like a forgotten nursery rhyme.
Hunters talk of a curse that befalls any who kill any beast with a streak of white fur. Soon after, they are found dead in their homes. Each day, there are fewer and fewer creatures to hunt.
Folks say that a faint laughter can be heard echoing out of wells all over the city, and that the echoes change to sobs at night.
The constellations have slowly started shifting in the night sky, forming unfamiliar patterns that have strangers and sages perplexed. Even the ambient seems disturbed.
An ancient tree at the heart of a sleepy village has suddenly withered and died, despite showing no signs of disease. After its trunk was cut, a shadowy hand was found at its core.

Statues have been weeping blood for months on end, and the wombs of every maiden have lain barren since. A single child has been the only exception, hidden away by elders overcome with fear and dread.
A foul tide is behaving oddly, displaying heightened aggression or fleeing from the entirety. Hunters talk of a shadowy figure that roams the Wood, calling to the animals.

Local streams have become riotous in recent weeks after multiple claims of a red-robed figure appearing in their children's dreams, uttering the same warning- A fire is coming and it will consume everything.

INT animals gain human intelligence for one day.
You create a magic eye that flies around under your control for INT turns. You can see through it as well as your normal eyes.
An object is frozen in time and space within an invulnerable crystal shell for INT turns.
INT + 1 objects are strongly magnetically attracted to each other if they come within 10'.
You can create illusory sounds that seem to come from INT directions of your choice.
INT creatures must loudly and clearly repeat everything you think. They are otherwise mute.
You and your possessions turn into an animal for up to INT days.
A creature is unable to form short-term memories for INT turns.
Roll INT + 1 d20s. After this point, when any creature you can see makes a check, use and discard one of the rolled results until they are all gone.
You switch bodies with a creature you touch for INT turns. If one body dies, the other dies as well.
A woman wearing a blue dress appears for INT hours. She will obey polite, safe requests.
INT humanoids believe they are close friends with you until proven otherwise.
A creature obeys a single, INT-word command that doesn’t harm it.
You are fluent in all languages for INT hours.
Plants within INT × 10' obey you. They move 5' per round.
You control your hex’s weather for INT hours.
Anything magical within line of sight glows and reveals its properties on request. Lasts 1 day or until you make INT requests.
INT body parts may be detached at will. You can still control them. Lasts until they are reattached.
You may alter the look of INT humanoids as long as they remain humanoid. Lasts until the subjects speak.
An object appears to be up to INT × 10' from its actual position.
Create INT fragile, porcelain copies of items you can see.
The ground shakes violently for INT rounds.
Your body can stretch up to INT × 10'.
Creates a wall of ice or fire INT × 40' long, 5' wide and 10' tall. The wall can curve however you want.
INT visible items teleport to your hands.
Fog spreads out in an INT × 10' radius from you. Fades in one turn.
INT creatures can alter their 'down' direction at will.
INT creatures become obsessed with possessing a visible item.
INT creatures have their movement speed tripled.
INT creatures start attacking each other for one turn or until one dies.
A creature can hear all sounds up to 120' away for INT turns.
Make INT objects hover 2' above the ground, frictionless. They can support the weight of up to INT people.
A creature enters a trance and will answer INT yes or no questions.
An ice layer spreads across a surface, up to INT × 10' in radius.
The gravity within INT × 10' of you triples.
INT objects within 10' of each other cannot be moved more than 10' apart from each other.
You can jump up to INT × 10'.
The air within INT × 10' of you becomes swimmable.
A door cannot be opened by mundane means for INT turns.
All magic is nullified while within INT × 10' of you.
A furnished house with INT rooms appears for 1 day. It has no food or gear and does not count as a safe haven.
Your pockets refill with marbles every round for INT rounds.
All creatures within INT × 10' of you are compelled to dance.
You and INT other touched creatures become mouse-sized.
INT illusory copies of you, under your control, appear.
A mirror becomes a gate to another mirror you touched today.
An INT × 40' wide sphere of total darkness appears.
INT willing creatures become inanimate, immobile objects of your choice for as long as they wish. They can still hear and see.
Your body and gear become living slime for INT turns.
INT creatures develop an intense hatred of violence unless attacked.
A coach scoops up INT creatures (who are outdoors) and deposits them in a random adjacent hex.
INT creatures become terrified of an object.
A pit 10' wide and INT × 10' deep opens in the ground.
An object grows to the size of an elephant for INT turns. If it is a creature, it is enraged.
The GM answers INT yes or no questions about an object.
An object of any size is pulled directly towards you with the force of INT men for one round.
An object of any size is pushed directly away from you with the force of INT men for one round.
INT unarmed skeletons rise from the ground to serve you.
You can hear the surface thoughts of creatures for INT turns.
INT + 1 objects are strongly magnetically repelled from each other if they come within 10'.
You can share the vision of a creature you touched today for INT turns.
Inanimate material acts like clay in your hands for INT turns.
INT creatures are invisible for as long as they can hold their breath (CON × 3 rounds).
All sound is deadened within 10' of you for INT turns.
Your body and gear become living smoke for INT turns.
In 10 minutes, a knight atop a giant snail rides into view. He may aid you for INT days if he finds you worthy. The snail cannot move faster than a walk.
A creature can smell all scents up to 120' away for INT turns.
Inanimate items sort themselves according to INT categories you set. The categories must be visually verifiable.
The spirit of a touched dead body appears and will answer INT questions (if it can).
A clearly unreal illusion appears under your control for INT days. It may be up to the size of a palace and has full motion and sound.
Cast this as a reaction to another spell of level INT or less being cast to make a temporary copy of it that you can cast within 1 day.
You can climb surfaces like a spider for INT turns.
You may summon or banish a 5' cube of earth 5 times per round for INT rounds. Cubes must be affixed to the earth or to other cubes.
A carved stone statue up to INT × 10' tall rises from the ground.
You become a swarm of crows, rats, or piranhas for INT turns. You only take damage from area effects.
You may mentally manipulate items (one at a time) up to 10 feet away for INT turns.
You can project your thoughts into a mind within INT hexes.
An object teleports to a clear patch of ground up to INT × 40' away from its origin point.
An object becomes the target of every spell cast within 120' of it for INT turns.
A thicket of trees and dense brush up to INT × 40' wide sprouts up over the course of one round.
An object disappears as it jumps INT turns into the future. When it returns, it destroys any matter in its space.

Time within INT × 10' of you goes 10 times slower than the rest of the world. Lasts 10 rounds (for you).
